column1: # One row per fixture: the case name, a tab, and text the fixture's FIRST
# diagnostic must contain. The case name is the folder for a nested fixture and
# the filename for a flat one.
# Asserting the message is the point. Asserting only that a fixture fails lets
# it pass while dying somewhere else entirely, which is what a fifth of this
# corpus was doing: a case written as `Employee co.lang.unit = { ... }` inside a
# file named after the rule stopped at the primary-declaration filename rules and
# never reached the rule it was named for. Every case below is pinned to the rule
# When a diagnostic is reworded, update the row in the same commit. A row that no
# longer matches is the test doing its job, not noise to route around.

column1: # Withdrawn cases, kept here so the intent is not lost.
#   future-fixity.fol. Both rules belong to the operator bootstrap surface, which
#   parseOperatorSource owns; an ordinary source file never reaches them, because
#   an @co.dap.operator annotation there may only overload.
#   Would pin "cannot specify precedence; parse properties belong only in the
#   "mode" out of the annotation, so the loop that reports a parse property in an
#   ordinary file never sees one. Restore this case once that is fixed.
#   Would pin the extra-field rule of the reserved package.fol source form.
#   and component.fol as reserved exact filenames, so package.fol classifies as an
#   ordinary <Name>.fol primary and parsePackageMetadataSourceFile is never
#   entered. Restore this case once that is fixed.
#   Would pin the Directive Placement rule for a library surface body, the path
#   parseLibraryMember owns. Unreachable: "co.lang.library" is absent from
#   scanlex.Builtin_Kinds, so it never scans as a kind token,
#   classifyCompilationUnitBySyntax never returns unitLibrary, and no library.fol
#   parses in any form. Restore this case once that is fixed.
